```{python}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

data_dir = ".." if os.path.exists("../students.csv") else "."
students = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, "students.csv"))
semesters = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, "semesters.csv"))
first_semester = semesters[semesters['semester'] == 1]

n_students = len(students)
n_faculties = students['faculty'].nunique()
mean_wb = round(first_semester['wellbeing'].mean(), 1)
```

## Sample

The sample included `{python} n_students` graduate students from
`{python} n_faculties` faculties. Their average wellbeing in the first
semester was `{python} mean_wb` on the
wellbeing index (0 to 100). @tbl-faculty shows wellbeing by faculty.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-faculty
#| tbl-cap: "Wellbeing in the first semester, by faculty."
merged = first_semester.merge(students, on='student_id')
summary_table = (
    merged.groupby('faculty')
    .agg(
        Students=('student_id', 'count'),
        Mean=('wellbeing', 'mean'),
        SD=('wellbeing', 'std')
    )
    .reset_index()
    .round(1)
)
summary_table.columns = ['Faculty', 'Students', 'Mean', 'SD']
summary_table
```

## Change over the programme

Wellbeing changed over the four semesters of the programme (@fig-wellbeing).
Differences are described with standardised effect sizes [@cohen1988], and all
results can be reproduced from the data and this document [@peng2011].

```{python}
#| label: fig-wellbeing
#| fig-cap: "Average wellbeing by semester."
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of average wellbeing over semesters 1 to 4."
trend = semesters.groupby('semester')['wellbeing'].mean().reset_index()

plt.figure(figsize=(6, 3.5))
plt.plot(trend['semester'], trend['wellbeing'], marker='o', linewidth=2, color='#1f77b4')
plt.xlabel("Semester")
plt.ylabel("Average wellbeing (0 to 100)")
plt.xticks([1, 2, 3, 4])
plt.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.5)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
